purpose: Phase 2 of reviews/markdown-conversion-plan.md: every class and element in search-textbook.html mapped to its Markdown source construct. Checked by tools/test-markdown-mapping.py.

statuses.native: Pandoc's own reader and HTML writer produce it unchanged.
statuses.filter: A Markdown convention rendered by the book's Lua filter (tools/markdown/book.lua) into the exact book markup.
statuses.derived: Built from chapter front matter, file order or a data file by the Markdown build. Not written in the Markdown body. New in this conversion: currently hand-maintained in the HTML.
statuses.generated: Produced by an existing generator (maintain.py, build-product-claims.py, build-glossary-hub.py). Never authored in Markdown.
statuses.template: Page shell in book/template.html: head, hero, navigation, scripts, footer.
statuses.raw: Inside a raw-HTML island: a bespoke diagram kept as HTML, in book/figures/<key>.html or a ```{=html} block.

constructs.markdown: Nothing. Built from file order: front matter nav is "both" (has a bar, is linked to; default for chapters, appendices and exercises), "target" (linked to only as the next item: the back-matter divider and the glossary) or "none". Titles: the h2 for chapters and back sections, the h2 before " — " for exercises, "Appendix X · " plus the h2 for appendices, the summary for the glossary; nav_title overrides.

constructs.markdown: :::: {.figure key=SLUG} — first paragraph is the title; then body blocks (an image paragraph, or a raw island); then ::: caption … ::: for the figcaption. Variant classes (.worked-figure, .evidence-card) and overrides (tag=div role=group, title-id, caption-id) are attributes on the figure div. ::: evidence-stack wraps figure divs natively.
constructs.notes: maintain.py assigns the figure number and fig-N-M id. Image srcset and sizes are derived from src when a .960.webp sibling exists; an image that does not follow the rule carries explicit attributes.

constructs.markdown: Pipe table with a caption line `: caption sentence`. Options go on a wrapper, ::: {.table scope="row" table-class="token-comparison"}, because Pandoc 3.1 reads no caption attributes. scope="row" makes each body row's first cell <th scope="row">, "col" gives header cells scope="col", "both" does both.
constructs.notes: Pandoc's own table output (caption element, header/odd row classes) is not used. maintain.py assigns the number and tbl-N-M id.

constructs.markdown: :::: {.figure .query-flow key=SLUG}: title paragraph, one ::: {.track} (optionally .five-step) per track holding a bullet list of `**Step name** description` items, then ::: caption. Arrows are added between steps.
constructs.notes: query-flow-step also appears inside the raw object-grid island; there it is part of the raw HTML.

constructs.markdown: ::: {.common-confusion label="IR terminology"} with an optional `#### Heading {#id}`. The filter emits <aside>, the label paragraph and aria-labelledby (heading id) or aria-label (label attribute). A div form (`tag=div`) covers div.orientation. ::: chapter-close has a fixed label, an ordered list and an optional ::: chapter-transition paragraph. Definition lists inside .distinction-map render each pair in a <div>. key-distinction-label is a paragraph class (see paragraph-class).
constructs.notes: Attributes: label, label-class (callout-label, key-distinction-label), label-id, aria-labelledby or aria-label overrides, tag="div" for div.orientation. A paragraph whose class also names an aside type (p.practice-callout) is written with tag="p". distinction-map-list is a definition list in ::: distinction-map-list; each pair is wrapped in a <div>.

constructs.markdown: ::: {.details} — the first paragraph is the summary, the rest is the body. Extra classes pass to <details>: ::: {.details .technical-note}.

A div with one class around exactly one block gives that class (and id and attributes) to the block: ::: {.worked-note} paragraph :::; ::: pull-quote around a > blockquote; ::: stage-key around a definition list. Paragraph ids use the same form: ::: {#id} paragraph :::.
constructs.notes: Also used by key-distinction-label, chapter-transition and exercise-deliverable, which are listed under their own constructs. worked-note outside raw islands only. p.practice-callout (one instance) uses this form with class practice-callout.

constructs.markdown: $…$ inline and $$…$$ display, as Pandoc Math; the filter writes MathJax delimiters back with the line breaks as given. A display-maths div is ::: {.math tag="div"} or ::: {.equation-scroll tag="div" …}; the paragraph form of equation-scroll has no tag.
constructs.notes: The book has no literal single dollar signs in prose, so tex_math_dollars is safe.

constructs.markdown: [d]{.var} renders <var>; likewise .small, .b, .output. [*text*]{.verdict} renders <em class="verdict">. term-mark is a link with attributes: [text](#term-x){.term-mark aria-describedby=… data-term=… data-def=…}.
constructs.notes: term-mark is native link-attribute syntax; it is listed here with the inline rules for convenience.

element_notes.ol: Write `#.` items or let the filter clear the list style; Pandoc otherwise adds type="1".
element_notes.li: An item that must carry an id (the 30 vendor questions) starts with []{#vendor-q01 .li-id}; the filter writes such a list itself, keeping the ids and any start number.
element_notes.br:
A hard line break (backslash at line end); the filter writes
with no following newline, which would otherwise add a space.
element_notes.dd:
Pandoc emits definitions without

for tight lists, matching the book.
element_notes.title: Also the SVG <title> element, which is raw.
element_notes.sup: Only footnote references use <sup> in the current book.
element_notes.pre: A fenced code block renders Pandoc's native <pre><code>, which is the book's markup.
element_notes.img: srcset and sizes are derived by the filter when a .960.webp sibling exists; an image whose srcset does not follow the rule carries it explicitly, and srcset="none" suppresses derivation.
